title: Module 0: How a Backend Works
mechanism: Trace browser, HTTP boundary, controller/service/data and response.
revisit_when: You cannot place a bug in the request path.

title: Module 1: JavaScript Fundamentals for Interviews
mechanism: Explain scope, values, references, closures and collection behavior.
revisit_when: Mutation, coercion or callback results surprise you.

title: Module 2: Asynchronous JavaScript
mechanism: Trace Promises, awaiting, scheduling, rejection and bounded concurrency.
revisit_when: Async work is missing, leaked or falsely assumed rolled back.

title: Module 3: TypeScript Fundamentals
mechanism: Separate static narrowing from runtime input validation.
revisit_when: A typed API trusts malformed external JSON.

title: Module 4: Node.js — What It Is and How It Works
mechanism: Explain Node execution, I/O, buffers/streams and process resources.
revisit_when: One CPU task or resource leak stalls unrelated traffic.

title: Module 5: Express.js and Backend Application Structure
mechanism: Trace Express middleware order, service boundaries and error flow.
revisit_when: Validation/auth/error handling executes in the wrong order.

title: Module 6: REST APIs and HTTP in Application Design
mechanism: Define method/status/representation, pagination and retry semantics.
revisit_when: A client and API disagree about success or replay safety.

title: Module 7: Authentication, Sessions, JWT and OAuth
mechanism: Trace credential transport, verification, expiry and revocation.
revisit_when: A login works but identity/session assumptions are unclear.

title: Module 8: API Security, Authorization and Multi-Tenancy
mechanism: Enforce resource/action/tenant policy at every relevant boundary.
revisit_when: Another tenant or a revoked user can access derived data.

title: Module 9: Webhooks, Payments and Reliable Integrations
mechanism: Protect payment/webhook effects with authentication and durable identity.
revisit_when: Duplicate or ambiguous events repeat business effects.

title: Module 10: Python Fundamentals for Backend Interviews
mechanism: Explain Python values, mutability, exceptions and coroutine execution.
revisit_when: Defaults, data types or async execution behave unexpectedly.

title: Module 11: Flask, FastAPI and Python Request Handling
mechanism: Distinguish framework request handling from blocking dependency work.
revisit_when: An async endpoint blocks or loses request-lifetime work.

title: Module 12: Django and Django REST Framework
mechanism: Trace Django/DRF validation, ORM/query work and permissions.
revisit_when: Framework defaults are mistaken for complete application policy.

title: Module 13: PostgreSQL in a Backend
mechanism: Use access patterns, constraints, plans and transactions deliberately.
revisit_when: Queries, pool waits or read-modify-write operations fail under load.

title: Module 14: MongoDB in a Backend
mechanism: Choose document boundaries, indexes and atomic/transactional updates.
revisit_when: Partial updates, duplicate identity or multi-document rules fail.

title: Module 15: Caching, Background Jobs and Data Ingestion
mechanism: Explain source truth, cache freshness, job identity and publication.
revisit_when: A retry, stale worker or expiry creates incorrect derived state.

title: Module 16: Docker Fundamentals
mechanism: Explain image/container, networks, volumes, configuration and readiness.
revisit_when: A container cannot reach dependencies or preserve data.

title: Module 17: Linux Deployment, Nginx and PM2
mechanism: Trace Linux process, reverse proxy, TLS, restart and drain behavior.
revisit_when: Deployment, trust or shutdown differs from local development.

title: Module 18: AWS and GCP Fundamentals for This Resume
mechanism: Separate IAM, service identity, networking, queue and storage boundaries.
revisit_when: A managed-service label hides an unresolved permission/failure rule.

title: Module 19: Git, CI/CD, Testing, Observability and Performance
mechanism: Link Git/CI gates, telemetry, performance evidence and rollback.
revisit_when: A test or benchmark claim lacks a reproducible boundary.

title: Module 20: React Fundamentals
mechanism: Explain render snapshots, state, keys, effects and request races.
revisit_when: The UI shows stale results or loses identity/state.

title: Module 21: Next.js, API Routes and Tailwind
mechanism: Separate Next.js runtime/render/cache boundaries and Tailwind styling.
revisit_when: Server/client code, hydration or cache scope leaks correctness.

title: Module 22: LLM and AI API Fundamentals
mechanism: Bound model/tool work, usage, structured output and evaluation.
revisit_when: A model result is trusted as permission or an unbounded workflow.

title: Module 23: RAG and Document Ingestion
mechanism: Trace source/chunk provenance, ingestion state and accepted evidence.
revisit_when: A citation or answer uses stale, missing or unauthorized content.

title: Module 24: Embeddings, Pinecone and pgvector
mechanism: Distinguish embedding/index configuration, scoped retrieval and recall.
revisit_when: A similarity score is mistaken for relevance or permission.

title: Module 25: LangChain, LangGraph and LlamaIndex
mechanism: Explain chain/workflow/agent state, checkpoints and replay.
revisit_when: A durable graph checkpoint repeats an external side effect.

title: Module 26: Neo4j and Graph-Backed Applications
mechanism: Anchor bounded graph queries and validate path/source scope.
revisit_when: Graph expansion crosses tenant or freshness boundaries.

title: Module 27: System-Design Bridge Through Your Load Balancer
mechanism: Defend placement, virtual nodes, health, overload and measured metrics.
revisit_when: Affinity, key balance and actual request load are conflated.

title: Module 28: Resume Project and Experience Deep-Dives
mechanism: Explain personal work and label reported, verified and proposed details.
revisit_when: A resume number or topology lacks original evidence.
